transcript:
Header:
2027-04-25 10:00 PDT · Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Morales (Redwood SE), Jared Liu (CTO - Nova Retail), Priya Shah (Head of ML - Nova), Carlos Mendes (Infra)
---
Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
Nova is evaluating expanding their Dedicated capacity with Redwood to add an extra GPU pool for peak holiday traffic, plus adding EU and APAC regions. Discussion covered pricing for committed capacity, SSO/SAML and KMS requirements, SOC2 and audit logs, benchmark plan, and proposed 12-month contract extension. Next steps and benchmarks agreed.
Topics: capacity upgrades; additional regions (EU, APAC); contract extension options; security & KMS; benchmark/testing window.
---
Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick checkin today, hope the time works for the nova crew.
[00:06] Jared: Yeah thanks Samir, this works. we've got Priya and Carlos here as well, so we'll go through the growth plan.
[00:12] Samir: Great. real quick agenda — capacity needs for Q3/Q4, additional regions, contract timing, any legal/security asks. Elena will jump into perf and benchmarks.
[00:22] Elena: Hey hi all, yeah hi. so i pulled the recent telemetry you sent, priya, and it looks like 95th percentile traffic spikes are about 2.2x of normal during promo windows. so you mentioned wanting a dedicated pool to cover that with headroom?
[00:36] Priya: yeah exactly. our holiday traffic historically spikes up, and with the new recommender + chat features we're planning bigger experiments. we're seeing longer seq lengths too — more multi-turn context — so kv cache is getting heavier.
[00:49] Carlos: and the infra ask is also about geography — EU data residency for a subset of customers plus APAC region support. currently everything's US east only.
[00:58] Elena: got it. so two asks: a dedicated fleet sized for peak RPS and seq length, and region expansion. Samir, do we want to run numbers?
[01:06] Samir: yeah, i sketched a couple of options — small dedicated pool, medium with autoscale, and a large reserved commitment with burst capacity. pricing differs  — reserved has best unit economics but needs a 12-mo commit.
[01:20] Jared: that's what i wanted to talk about. what's the delta between hosted overage vs dedicated commit? we ran some numbers and concerned about cost predictability.
[01:28] Samir: rough ballpark, dedicated reserved is ~30-40% lower per-token equivalent compared to burst on hosted for sustained throughput. for short bursts hosted is fine but you pay more. we can model your 90-day forecast to show break-even.
[01:39] Priya: quick Q on compliance — would the private control plane (VPC) be available with the dedicated offering? we need KMS integration and audit logs for SOC 2.
[01:47] Elena: yes. dedicated supports VPC peering or private link, KMS/HSM integration for key management, and we keep audit logs with retention options. note: some of the names in the doc are autogenerated so sometimes the transcriber says K M S as letters, sorry.
[02:00] Carlos: cool. any network constraints we should know? we currently do TLS to public endpoints but we can set up a VPC peering. also latency to APAC is a concern.
[02:10] Samir: for APAC we recommend colocating a small pool in ap-southeast-1 or ap-northeast-1 depending on traffic. EU would be eu-west-1 ideally. each region has overhead for base capacity but cut down tail latency.
[02:21] Jared: if we add EU and APAC, how do rollouts work? can we do canary and auto-fallback to US region?
[02:28] Elena: yes, you can route by policy — latency-first for EU users hitting EU model, and fallback to US if capacity is saturated. we also support weighted rollouts and canary cluster configs.
[02:38] Priya: benchmarks — we'd like to run a two-day benchmark simulating peak holiday load with our prompt sets. what's the typical setup?
[02:45] Elena: we can provision a staging dedicated pool, run your traffic replay for 48 hours. we'll gather latency p50/p95/p99, token cost, effective throughput. note that our inference runtime does continuous batching and kv cache — you'll see improved unit economics in production vs naive replays.
[03:00] Carlos: can we get example perf numbers for the model family? we currently use a 7B variant and a 70B for heavy queries.
[03:07] Elena: 7B at medium quant runs great on A10-style GPUs, 70B needs v100/8 or ampere class. for cost control we recommend quantized 70B with offloading or sharded KV caches. i'll include the recommended SKU matrix in the followup.
[03:20] Jared: ok. about contract — we come up for renewal in July. if we sign for 12 months extension with added regions and a reserved pool, can you lock pricing?
[03:29] Samir: yes, we can do a contract amendment to extend term and add committed GPUs. pricing lock for committed capacity is standard; we'll include inflation clauses but we can offer a fixed unit rate for the term.
[03:40] Priya: any workaround for internal procurement? our legal team asks for SOC2 Type II evidence and penetration test reports.
[03:47] Samir: we have SOC2 docs and recent pen test summary; i'll attach the security pack. also audit log retention and SSO/SAML metadata — we can provide those.
[03:57] Carlos: can we get a copy of the network diagram for private deployment? also the KMS integration flow.
[04:02] Samir: yes, i'll share VPC templated diagram and KMS flow. Carlos, if you share your network CIDRs we can sketch peering plan.
[04:10] Jared: price sensitivity — we need to show finance the ROI. Priya, can you share predicted q3/q4 token growth?
[04:16] Priya: i'll export a 90-day forecast — average seq length, percent multi-turn, and peak RPS; i'll get that to you by monday. sorry, by monday meaning 2027-04-26.
[04:28] Elena: for the benchmark itself, small caveat — synthetic replays don't perfectly capture KV cache warmup. we recommend a warmup phase before measuring steady-state. sometimes the transcriber reads kv cache as kv cash in the notes.
[04:40] Carlos: haha yeah we've seen that. on the security front, we also need support for customer-managed keys, not just redwood-managed KMS.
[04:46] Samir: customer-managed keys supported for Private and Dedicated with VPC option. HSM integrations are possible depending on provider. i'll note that as a must-have in the amendment.
[04:56] Jared: can we get a sample contract amendment showing added regions and a commit for 8 GPUs with monthly autoscale up to 12 for bursts?
[05:03] Samir: yes, we'll draft an amendment with the three-tier option: 8 reserved GPUs, autoscale to 12, or 12 reserved for a deeper discount. we'll include a pricing table.
[05:13] Priya: one more item — we'd like per-route telemetry and token-level cost breakdowns so our product team can attribute spend. is that available?
[05:20] Elena: yes, redwood console provides per-route and per-model dashboards, token cost by route, and tracing hooks. retention tiers can be adjusted for compliance.
[05:28] Carlos: what about SLOs? we need 99.9 for public endpoints and 99.5 for backend batch jobs.
[05:34] Samir: SLA for dedicated pools is configurable and we can commit to 99.9 for the reserved capacity. for hosted, different tiers exist. we'll include proposed SLA language in the amendment.
[05:44] Jared: cool. ok recap?
[05:46] Samir: recap — nova wants capacity for holiday peaks, add EU and APAC regions, 12-month contract extension with committed GPUs; run a 48-hour benchmark on staging, provide SOC2 and pen test docs, and draft contract amendment.
[05:58] Priya: yep, and we'll provide the 90-day traffic forecast and prompt sets.
[06:02] Carlos: i'll send network diagram and KMS contacts.
[06:05] Samir: great. i'll send the pricing tiers and amendment draft by tuesday 2027-04-27; Elena will schedule the benchmark and send runbook by 2027-04-29.
[06:15] Jared: thanks all, that works.
[06:16] Samir: any final questions?
[06:17] Priya: none from me. thanks.
[06:18] Elena: quick note — during the benchmark we recommend using a mix of short-chat and long-context sessions to reflect real load.
[06:24] Samir: perfect. thanks everyone. end of call.
